clue.text: British queen losing articles of clothing

indicators.note: a queen who is losing something has letters taken away from her name

parts.note: Boadicea was the queen of the Iceni who rose against Roman Britain
two indefinite articles, each the letter A

explanation.surface: A British queen sheds some of her garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like part of 'articles of clothing', but it stands for the two A's dropped from BOADICEA; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the close-fitting upper part of a dress, a garment in its own right.

clue.text: Produce fine by including foreign currency

indicators.note: the word by is split open so that it holds the currency within it

parts.note: taken as written
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: Someone pays a fine by producing money from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' just links the definition to the wordplay. 'Fine' here is the noun: in French, a fine is a brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine (French) is a good-quality brandy, as in fine champagne cognac.

clue.text: Finish off my birthday dancing to wild song

indicators.note: the remaining letters dance about into a new order
to finish off a phrase is to cut away its final letter

explanation.surface: At the end of a birthday party, everyone dances to a raucous song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' removes the last Y of MY BIRTHDAY, leaving MYBIRTHDA; 'dancing' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dithyramb was an ecstatic choral hymn to Dionysus, so any wild, impassioned song or chant.

clue.text: Chocolate maker's business without an accountant

indicators.note: used in the old sense of outside, so the business wraps round the rest

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
the indefinite article as the letter A
CA, chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A chocolate firm getting by with no accountant on the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean 'lacking', but it is the old use meaning 'outside'. CA is a chartered accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacao beans and the cacao tree are the source from which chocolate is made.

clue.text: Marks a combination of courses with little variation

parts.words: combination of courses with little variation
parts.note: compass courses SSE, SSE and S, three headings barely different from one another

explanation.surface: An examiner grades a mixed bag of subjects with hardly any spread in the results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' sounds academic, but means compass headings: SSE, SSE and S, which differ only slightly, follow A.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark is to grade or evaluate a piece of work, which is what an examiner does.

clue.text: Incredible soak

definitions.meaning: to leave something soaking in liquid

explanation.definitionFit: Steep means exorbitant or far-fetched, and as a verb means to immerse something in liquid.

clue.text: Charmed way in which daughter succeeds

indicators.note: to succeed is to come after, so the daughter follows the way in

parts.note: an entrance is a way in

explanation.surface: A daughter finds an enchanting route into the family business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeds' suggests inheriting, but it puts D after ENTRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is enchanted or spellbound has been charmed.

clue.text: Bit of a mishap emptying jelly mould

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A small accident in the kitchen leaves the jelly mould empty.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'miSHAP Emptying'. 'Shape' is an old word for a moulded jelly or blancmange.
explanation.definitionFit: A shape is a moulded dessert such as a jelly or blancmange, and also the form a mould gives.

clue.text: Epithet for son of Daedalus after Browning?

definitions.text: Epithet for son of Daedalus after Browning?

parts.words: Epithet for son of Daedalus after Browning?
parts.note: Icarus, son of Daedalus, flew too near the sun; browning as in tanning makes the description fit him and any sunbather

explanation.surface: A literary note on what the poet Browning called a mythical boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browning' looks like the poet Robert Browning, but it means going brown in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Icarus' wax wings melted near the sun, and skin gone brown from the sun is described this way.

clue.text: Private on duty list without a bunk

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece written on another sits above it, so the soldier comes first

parts.note: Tommy (Tommy Atkins) is slang for a private soldier in the British army

indicators.note: the duty list is taken without, that is minus, the letter named

parts.note: a rota is a list of who is on duty when
the letter A

explanation.surface: A soldier on the duty roster finds he has no bed to sleep in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk' looks like a bed but is short for bunkum, nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk (from bunkum) means nonsense or rubbish, the same as tommyrot.

clue.text: Plant producing so-called aesthetic clog

indicators.note: what something is called is how it is spoken, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: arty means aesthetic, pretentiously artistic; choke means clog or block

explanation.surface: A garden plant that manages to block things up in an artistic way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clog' looks like a wooden shoe, but is the verb: to choke.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a thistle-like plant grown for its edible flower head.

clue.text: File and drill

definitions.meaning: a file is a line of people one behind another
to drill is to coach or school someone

explanation.definitionFit: A train is a procession or line, and to train someone is to drill them in a skill.

clue.text: Place where inmates can sit or may do cooking

indicators.note: cooking the books means falsifying, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Prisoners may sit in the room or do their cooking there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' looks like part of the inmates' activities, but it scrambles OR MAY DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A day room in a hospital or prison is a communal lounge where residents sit during the day.

clue.text: Period of stability recently in Pyrenean tourist centre

indicators.note: one word sits in another, so the tourist centre holds it

parts.note: Pau is a resort town in the foothills of the French Pyrenees
late means recently, as in 'of late'

explanation.surface: A town in the Pyrenees has lately enjoyed a calm spell.
explanation.walkthrough: A plateau is also high flat land, which suits the mountains in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is a phase where something levels off and stays steady.

clue.text: Job for composer of sacred music making a huge amount

definitions.text: Job for composer of sacred music
definitions.meaning: writing a Mass, the setting of the Eucharist, is a church composer's work
manufacturing goods in vast numbers on a production line

explanation.definitionFit: Producing a Mass is a church composer's task; the phrase also means factory manufacture on a vast scale.

clue.text: Abrasive noise of Cockney bird

indicators.note: a word as a Cockney Londoner would say it, with the long a coming out like a long i

parts.note: sandpaper is an abrasive sheet for smoothing wood

explanation.surface: A Cockney bird makes a harsh scratchy call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' looks like Cockney slang for a girl, but is the definition. A Cockney (East Londoner) says 'paper' as 'piper'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sandpiper is a wading bird of shorelines and mudflats.

clue.text: Note, say, on card to crowd around speaker

indicators.note: say signals the note is to be heard rather than spelt as written

parts.note: doh is the first note of the tonic sol-fa scale
a card is an eccentric, a nut

explanation.surface: Musical note written on a card for the crowd around a lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Commons a doughnut is the ring of MPs gathered round the member speaking so as to look well on television.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped cluster of politicians around whoever is speaking is called by this pastry's name.

clue.text: It has to be blown up in middle of the Underground

definitions.text: It has to be blown up

parts.note: inner means in the middle, central
the Tube is London's Underground railway

explanation.surface: Something in the middle of the London Underground has to be blown up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a bomb threat, but 'blown up' means inflated.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable rubber tube inside a tyre must be pumped full of air.

clue.text: A detective superintendent found person using drug

parts.note: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, stands for detectives
a head is a superintendent or person in charge

explanation.surface: A senior police officer has tracked down a drug user.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detective superintendent' looks like a single police rank, but the two words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An acidhead is a slang term for a habitual user of LSD.

clue.text: One of the sweets of office?

definitions.text: One of the sweets of office?

parts.words: One of the sweets of office?
parts.note: the perks of high office read as a dessert, the sweet course, named after the government's top ministers

explanation.surface: One of the perks that come with holding high office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweets' looks like perks but is a pudding; the Cabinet is the group of senior government ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamed sponge with dried fruit, served as dessert, takes its name from the ministers' council.

clue.text: Lack of pretensions in rising inventor

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: side means pretentiousness or airs, so no side is a lack of it

explanation.surface: A modest inventor who has risen without putting on airs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' (British informal) means affected superiority or airs.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison, who patented the phonograph and light bulb, is a famous inventor.

clue.text: No longer in use, slate is blank

parts.note: dead means defunct, no longer in use
to slate and to pan both mean to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: An old slate no longer used is left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slate' looks like the writing tablet, but is the verb to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank, expressionless face is said to be deadpan.

clue.text: Is almost touching — except when outside

indicators.note: one word is placed outside another, so the word for when goes round

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
but means except, as in 'all but one'

explanation.surface: Something nearly touches, except when it is out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' seems to belong to the surface, but it is the container signal. 'almost' fits the definition: to abut is to touch only at a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that adjoin or border each other lie edge to edge.

clue.text: Saltpetre container upset by engineers

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, the letters read upwards

parts.note: a tin is a container
RE, the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Army engineers knock over a can of saltpetre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TIN to NIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is potassium nitrate, the old chemical name for saltpetre.

definitions.meaning: an English gold coin of the Middle Ages
fine as in admirable, grand, of high character

explanation.definitionFit: The noble was a medieval English gold coin, and the adjective means splendid or of high quality.

clue.text: Stock English joke

parts.note: a quip is a witty joke

explanation.surface: A stock English joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like an adjective (a stock joke) but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To stock a place is to supply or furnish it with what is needed.

clue.text: Real attack of depression for Tories

parts.note: true means real, genuine
the blues is a fit of low spirits

explanation.surface: Conservatives suffering a genuine fit of gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of the British Conservative Party, the Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: Staunch, loyal Conservatives are called by this name, blue being the party colour.

clue.text: What's merited by King Rat?

indicators.note: by means beside, so the king stands next to what is merited

parts.note: a desert, as in just deserts, is what someone has earned
ER, as in Edward Rex

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a monarch called Rat has earned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Rat' reads as a title, but 'King' gives ER and 'Rat' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is someone who abandons their side, like rats leaving a sinking ship.

clue.text: Downgrade estate to auditor, possibly

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is as heard by the ear

parts.note: a demesne is a landed estate

explanation.surface: An estate's value is lowered by the accountant checking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant, but means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower or degrade their standing.
